answer.worked:
Using the added assumption $g(0)=-1$, the graphs give
$$\begin{align*}
\operatorname{dom}(f)&=(-\infty,0)\cup(0,2),\\
\operatorname{range}(g)&=[-1,3),\\
\operatorname{range}(g)\cap\operatorname{dom}(f)&=[-1,0)\cup(0,2).
\end{align*}$$
The allowable inputs satisfy $g(x)<2$ and $g(x)\ne0$. The graph gives $g(x)<2$ for $-3<x<3$, while $g(x)=0$ at $x=-1$ and $x=1$.
$$\operatorname{dom}(f\circ g)=(-3,-1)\cup(-1,1)\cup(1,3).$$
For the range, read the outputs of $f$ on the two accessible input intervals:
$$\begin{align*}
f([-1,0))&=(-\infty,0],\\
f((0,2))&=[1,\infty).
\end{align*}$$
The endpoint $0$ is included because $f(-1)=0$, and the minimum $1$ is included because $f(1)=1$.
$$\operatorname{range}(f\circ g)=(-\infty,0]\cup[1,\infty).$$
